'''Reza Moridi''' ({{langx|fa|رضا مریدی}}; born {{circa|1945}}) is a former politician in [[Ontario]], Canada. He was a [[Ontario Liberal Party|Liberal]] member of the [[Legislative Assembly of Ontario]] from 2007 to 2018 who represented the riding of [[Richmond Hill (provincial electoral district)|Richmond Hill]]. He served as a cabinet minister in the government of [[Kathleen Wynne]]. He was the first [[Iranian-Canadian]] elected to legislature <ref name="YorkRegion.com">{{cite web |title=Moridi announces nomination for provincial Liberal party in Richmond Hill |url=https://www.yorkregion.com/news-story/7162475-moridi-announces-nomination-for-provincial-liberal-party-in-richmond-hill |publisher=Kim Zarzour from YorkRegion.com |date=Feb 28, 2017}}</ref> and appointed as a Cabinet minister in Canada.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The New Wynne Ministry |url=https://www.tvo.org/article/the-new-wynne-ministry |publisher=TVontario, Steve Paikin|date=Feb 12, 2013}}</ref>

==Background==
Moridi was born in [[Urmia]], capital of [[West Azerbaijan Province]] in [[Azerbaijan (Iran)|northwest]] [[Iran]]. He grew up in [[Urmia]], attended [[Alborz High School]] in Tehran and graduated from [[Tehran University]] with BSc and MSc degrees in Physics. He continued his education in the UK and obtained MTech and PhD degrees from [[Brunel University]] in London. He received an Honorary Doctorate from Odlar Yurdu University, Baku, Azerbaijan.

For his contributions to physics and engineering, Moridi was elected Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] and Fellow of the Institution of Engineering and Technology of the UK. In recognition of his contributions to the understanding of nuclear materials and radiation, the Canadian Nuclear Society presented him with the Education and Communication Award. Also, in recognition of his contributions to the profession of Health Physics, the [[Health Physics Society|Health Physics Society of the United States]] presented him with the Fellow Award. Moridi has received numerous awards and recognitions for his extensive community and humanitarian work.<ref name="Mackenzie Health Foundation">{{cite news |title=CELEBRATING THE ACHIEVEMENTS OF DR. REZA MORIDI |url=http://www.mackenziehealthfoundation.ca/event/celebrating-the-achievements-of-dr-reza-moridi | publisher=TVO|date=Oct 12, 2018}}</ref>

Prior to entering into politics, he was a Chartered Engineer and Chartered Physicist. He worked for 17 years at the Radiation Safety Institute of Canada where he was the Vice-President and Chief Scientist. He also worked in the electrical industry as an executive and in academia as a professor and administrator.

== Politics ==
[[File:RezaMoridi.jpg|thumb|Moridi's campaign office]]
Moridi ran as the [[Ontario Liberal Party|Liberal]] candidate in the [[2007 Ontario general election|2007 provincial election]] in the riding of [[Richmond Hill (provincial electoral district)|Richmond Hill]]. He defeated [[Progressive Conservative Party of Ontario|Progressive Conservative]] Alex Yuan by 5,329 votes.<ref name="2007 results">{{cite web |url=http://elections.on.ca/NR/rdonlyres/AB409CCD-84F3-46FA-B3BD-39AB659EFC2D/0/SummaryofValidBallotsCastforEachCandidate.pdf |title=Summary of Valid Ballots Cast for Each Candidate |publisher=Elections Ontario |date=October 10, 2007 |page=13 (xxii) |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091007160233/http://www.elections.on.ca/NR/rdonlyres/AB409CCD-84F3-46FA-B3BD-39AB659EFC2D/0/SummaryofValidBallotsCastforEachCandidate.pdf |archive-date=October 7, 2009 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> He was re-elected in [[2011 Ontario general election|2011]],<ref name="2011 results">{{cite web |url=http://elections.on.ca/NR/rdonlyres/7849B894-4C4F-490E-9E8C-271BCF0C0D4D/5712/SummaryofvalidvotescastforeacndGE2011.pdf |title=Summary of Valid Ballots Cast for Each Candidate |publisher=Elections Ontario |date=October 6, 2011 |page=15 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130330163815/http://elections.on.ca/NR/rdonlyres/7849B894-4C4F-490E-9E8C-271BCF0C0D4D/5712/SummaryofvalidvotescastforeacndGE2011.pdf |archive-date=March 30, 2013 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> and [[2014 Ontario general election|2014]].<ref name="2014 results">{{cite web |title=General Election by District: Richmond Hill |publisher=Elections Ontario |date=June 12, 2014 |url=http://wemakevotingeasy.ca/en/general-election-district-results.aspx?d=075}}</ref> Moridi was defeated in the 2018 Provincial Election by Conservative Member of Provincial Parliament [[Daisy Wai]]. He intended to contest his former seat as a Member of Provincial Parliament for Richmond Hill in four years in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yorkregion.com/news-story/8659014-pc-party-s-daisy-wai-unseats-liberal-reza-moridi-in-richmond-hill/|title=PC party's Daisy Wai unseats Liberal Reza Moridi in Richmond Hill|last=Zarzour|first=Kim|date=2018-06-08|website=YorkRegion.com|language=en-CA|access-date=2019-02-10}}</ref> Last year in 2020, Moridi formally announced that he will not going to run in the next election.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-01|title=Roqe - Episode 123 - Dr. Reza Moridi (from 57:51 to 58:56)|url=https://www.youtube.com/embed/Ge_l7xbivGg?start=3471|access-date=2021-07-01|website=www.youtube.com}}</ref>

During the [[Dalton McGuinty]] government he served as [[Parliamentary Assistant]] to the Ministers of [[Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities (Ontario)|Training, Colleges and Universities]], [[Ministry of Research and Innovation (Ontario)|Research and Innovation]] and [[Ministry of Energy (Ontario)|Energy]]. When [[Kathleen Wynne]] took over as Premier in 2013, she appointed Moridi to her cabinet as [[Ministry of Research and Innovation (Ontario)|Ministry of Research and Innovation]].<ref name="2013WynneCab">{{cite news |title=Ontario's new cabinet |newspaper=Waterloo Region Record |location=Kitchener, Ont |date=February 12, 2013 |page=A3}}</ref> After the 2014 election she assigned him the additional role of [[Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities (Ontario)|Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities]].<ref name="2014WynneCab">{{cite news |title=Kathleen Wynne warns financial cupboard is bare |url=https://www.thestar.com/news/queenspark/2014/06/24/ontario_premier_kathleen_wynnes_new_cabinet_unveiled.html |author1=Richard Brennan |author2=Robert Benzie |author3=Rob Ferguson |newspaper=Toronto Star |date=June 24, 2014}}</ref> On June 13, 2016, Moridi's cabinet role was reduced to a renamed portfolio of Minister of Research, Innovation and Science.<ref name="2016WynneCab">{{cite news |title=Kathleen Wynne's shuffled cabinet features 40% women |url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/ontario-cabinet-changes-1.3632476 |publisher=CBC News |date=June 13, 2016}}</ref> He also served as Chair of the Cabinet Committee on Education, Skills and Economy.

=== Contributions during Public Service ===
In 2015, Moridi launched modernization of the Ontario Students Assistance Program (OSAP) by making tuition free for students from low and middle income families and helped establish York University campus in Markham, e-Campus in Toronto and initiated the process of modernizing the university funding formula and the first ever stand-alone French language university in Ontario.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.ontario.ca/maesd/en/2015/09/ontario-modernizing-financial-aid-for-students.html|title=Ontario Modernizing Financial Aid for Students|website=news.ontario.ca|language=en|access-date=2015-01-15}}</ref>

He signed MOUs with countries such as China, Germany, Czech Republic, UK, Korea, Israel, Denmark, Turkey and Jordan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newswire.ca/fr/news-releases/ontario-universities-minister-head-to-turkey-to-strengthen-international-partnerships-516588611.html|title=Ontario universities, Minister head to Turkey to strengthen international partnerships|website=www.newswire.ca|language=en|access-date=2014-12-01}}</ref> He led Science and Technology missions to USA (four times), China (twice), Korea, Germany (twice), Czech Republic, Israel (twice), West Bank (twice), Jordan, Turkey, Armenia and Azerbaijan and led Nuclear Energy delegations to China and Korea.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/national/education/universities-should-expand-international-reputation-ontario-minister-says/article20526137/|title=Universities should expand international reputation, Ontario minister says|website=ww.theglobeandmail.com|date=10 September 2014 |language=en|access-date=2014-09-10}}</ref>

=== Voluntary Community Service since departure from politics ===

Since he left politics, Moridi has been serving on the following volunteer positions:
* Senior Fellow, Massey College, University of Toronto <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.masseycollege.ca/2020/06/17/announcing-the-2020-2021-incoming-senior-members-to-massey-college/|title=ANNOUNCING THE 2020-2021 INCOMING SENIOR MEMBERS TO MASSEY COLLEGE|website=masseycollege.ca|language=en|access-date=2022-04-16}}</ref>
* Chair of Dean's Special Advisory Board, York University Faculty of Science <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yorku.ca/science/about/strategic-plan/deans-special-advisory-board/|title=York University, Faculty of Science, Dean's Special Advisory Board|website=yorku.ca|language=en|access-date=2022-04-16}}</ref>
* Chair, Board of Directors, Radiation Safety Institute of Canada <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://radiationsafety.ca/who-we-are/|title=Radiation Safety Institute of Canada's Board of Directors|website=radiationsafety.ca|language=en|access-date=2022-04-16}}</ref>
* Chair, Honorary Advisory Board, Canada Innovative SMEs Association <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://canada-isa.org/about-us/#our-team|title=Canada Innovative SMEs Association's honorary Advisory Board|website=canada-isa.org|language=en|access-date=2022-04-16}}</ref>
* Chair, Board of Honorary Mentors, Outstanding Teenagers Leadership Foundation <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.otlf.ca/board-of-honorary-mentors|title=The Outstanding Teenager Leadership Foundation (OTLF)Board of Honorary Mentors|website=otlf.ca|language=en|access-date=2022-04-16}}</ref>
* Trustee, Royal Canadian Institute for Science <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rciscience.ca/executive-board|title=Royal Canadian Institute for Science's Board Members|website=rciscience.ca|language=en|access-date=2022-04-16|archive-date=28 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028185908/https://www.rciscience.ca/executive-board|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Trustee, Canadian Society of Iranian Engineers, and Architects <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mohandes.com/board-of-trustees/|title=Mohandes (The Canadian Society of Iranian Engineers and Architects) Board of Trustees|website=mohandes.com|language=en|access-date=2022-04-16}}</ref>
* Honorary Governor, Mon Sheong Foundation <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.monsheong.org/about-us/our-people/honorary-governors/|title=Mon Sheong Foundation's Honorary Governors|website=monsheong.org|language=en|access-date=2022-04-16}}</ref>
* Advisory Board, Yara Leadership Society <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yarasociety.com/who-we-are/|title=Yara Leadership Society's Advisory Board|website=yarasociety.com|language=en|access-date=2022-04-16}}</ref>

=== Awards and recognition ===
On October 12, 2018, the Iranian community of the Greater Toronto Area organized a tribute dinner honouring Reza Moridi where in recognition of his service to the Town of Richmond Hill, the Town named one of the streets “Urmia Avenue” -  after the ancient city of Urmia in Iran where Moridi was born.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yorkregion.com/news-story/9060423-richmond-hill-names-street-after-former-mpp-s-birthplace-in-iran/|title=Richmond Hill names street after former MPP's birthplace in Iran|last=Wang|first=Sheila|date=2018-12-03|website=YorkRegion.com|language=en-CA|access-date=2019-02-23}}</ref>

==Human rights==
Moridi has been active in support of human rights in his homeland Iran.  In 2009, he presented a petition to the legislature regarding the violation of human rights in Iran in the aftermath of the 2009 presidential election.<ref>{{YouTube|hbAQXW32CCQ|Reza Moridi's petition regarding "Human Rights on Sept 14, 2009}}</ref> He advocated for the passing of the legislation in the House of Commons of Canada on June 5, 2013, that proclaimed massacre of political prisoner in Iran by the order of Ayatollah Khomeini during the summer of 1988, was a [[crimes against humanity|crime against humanity]].  He also introduced a petition that asked the Federal Minister of Foreign Affairs to intervene on [[Saeed Malekpour]]'s behalf and appeal to the government of Iran to free him.<ref>{{cite news |title=Iran sentences Richmond Hill resident to death |url=http://www.postcity.com/Richmond-Hill-Post/January-2011/Iran-sentences-Richmond-Hill-resident-to-death |newspaper=Post City Magazine}}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|jPCCZrKHlfg|Reza Moridi reading a petition to the Legislative Assembly}}</ref>

In May 2010, he read a statement in praise of the [[Republic of Azerbaijan]] in honour of the nation's anniversary in which he called the current government of Azerbaijan "a secular democratic republic".<ref>{{YouTube|UNVXp9kadyw|Reza Moridi, Liberal MPP (Richmond Hill, Ontario) comments about Azerbaijan at the Legislative Assembly of Ontario, Canada, May 30, 2010}}.</ref>
